text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- Gazeta learned unofficially that President Aleksander Kwasniewski will call for dismissal of Zbigniew Siemiatkowski, the minister in charge of the security service, over remarks about expected provocations by Russian special services.

- Daewoo announced that all those who scrap their old cars between February 20 and March 31 will be able to buy a Daewoo-FSO Polonez with a 1,900 zloty discount or a Nexia with a discount of 2,300 to 2,600 zlotys.

- Drivers who cause a lot of accidents may from next month have to pay three times as much as others for obligatory civil liability insurance, said Anatol Adamski, director of the insurance department in the finance ministry.
- The Demoskop polling institute found that consumer sentiment improved in February, which is unusual for this time of year when sentiment usually either falls or is unchanged.

- Deputy Treasury Minister Leszek Juchniewicz said that if a firm is found which is ready to pay double the amount offered by the Franco-Polish Hachette-Wydawcy Prasy consortium for a stake in Poland's Ruch SA press distributor, and signs the same guarantees, this would be a suitable partner for talks.

- After joining the European Union Poland will have to radically increase sales tax on liquid fuels and other energy sources. This means that in a few years petrol and diesel prices will be twice as high as now.
- In January, 88 companies listed on the Warsaw bourse had net earnings of 150 million zlotys net, 16 percent less than a year earlier. This was due in part to worse results from banks.
- Krakow city authorities will shortly discuss a further issue of municipal bonds in two series, one for 25 million zlotys and one for 30 million.

- Subscriptions ended yesterday for shares in electrode maker ZEW SA. Most of the shares will probably be taken up by investors and the final issue price per share is likely to be around 40 to 45 zlotys.
- Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy in Lodz in two post-session lots sold 5.65 percent of shares in clothing maker Elpo. The bank is Elpo's principal shareholder.
